posts.content:
The next frontier in AI is not just a smarter model. It’s an agent that can be trusted to act.

The shift is clear: from single-model prompts to multi-agent systems that use tools, coordinate workflows, carry context, and take action in the real world.
But capability is moving faster than reliability.

An agent that can execute a transaction, change production infrastructure, or act on someone’s behalf needs more than a great model. It needs AI ready APIs, open standards for identity, permissions, observability, recovery, security, and governance.

That’s why I’m excited to share that Postman has joined the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a Linux Foundation sub-foundation helping build the open-source foundation for agentic AI.

AAIF already brings together core building blocks for the emerging agent ecosystem including MCP, and AGENTS.md to advance interoperable tools, standards, and community-led innovation.

For Postman, membership is the starting point not the outcome. We joined AAIF to contribute to the work.

APIs are becoming the action layer for AI agents: how they discover capabilities, call services, access data, and complete workflows. The next generation of APIs must therefore be designed not only for developers, but for secure, governed, observable agent behavior.

We plan to contribute actively where the hard production questions are being solved:
• Reliability and recovery when agents fail mid-workflow
• Traceability and auditability of agent decisions
• Identity, delegation, permissions, and cross-domain trust
• Secure agent-to-API interactions and multi-step business processes

The best agentic systems will not win because they are the most autonomous.

They will win because they are the most trustworthy.

Open source is how we make that trust portable, inspectable, and available to everyone. We’re excited to help build it with AAIF and the broader community.

#AgenticAI #AI #OpenSource #APIs #MCP #Postman #LinuxFoundation #AIInfrastructure
